title: Out of memory after data growth
story: Batch size grows from 60 to 180 MiB after 20 s; the 128 MiB limit OOM-kills every job. Expected heal: raise memory.

args.summary: Raised worker memory limit from 128m to 384m to accommodate growing batch sizes (observed 180 MiB batch causing RSS 131-149 MiB, exceeding the 128 MiB limit) and stop repeated OOM kills.

timeline.note: watching for 3× the crash interval (10–60) s with no crash or OOM

timeline.thought:
ROOT CAUSE: The worker was repeatedly OOM-killed (exit 137, oom_killed: true, 3 restarts in ~1.5s) because its batch size grew from 60 MiB to 180 MiB on job 11 ("job 11: loading batch (180 MiB)"), pushing process RSS to 131–149 MiB against the container's 128 MiB memory limit ("rss 138/149/145/131 MiB > limit 128 MiB"), causing a crash loop on restart since the oversized job is retried each time.

CHANGE: Raised the worker container memory limit from 128m to 384m (set_resources + apply_fix), giving ~2x headroom above the observed 180 MiB batch plus runtime overhead, while keeping replicas at 1 (job partitioning not supported) and cpus unchanged (CPU usage was low: avg 1.5%, peak 4%, not the bottleneck).

GUARDRAILS: Within policy — set_memory is an allowed action, 384m ≤ max_memory (512m) and ≤ max_total_memory (1g) for this single-replica service; replicas unchanged at 1 (min=max=1); dry-run validation returned ok:true with no violations.

FOLLOW-UP: Monitor mem_peak_mb over the next few nightly runs — notes indicate batch size "grows with customer data," so if batches trend toward/above ~300 MiB, proactively raise memory again (up to the 512m cap) or ask the owning team to add batch-size capping/chunking in the worker code, since memory limits alone won't scale indefinitely with unbounded batch growth.
